steps.title: Money that is ready at once
steps.body: An [[emergency-fund]] is money for surprises. It pays your costs if a job ends or something breaks. It does not need to grow. It needs to be there at once. Then you do not have to sell investments or borrow money in a hurry. People count it in months of costs.

steps.prompt: A household spends €2,800 a month. How big is an emergency fund for 3 months?
steps.reveal: 3 × €2,800 = €8,400. You count an emergency fund in months of costs, not as a round number. If an income stops, it gives you time to find a new one.

steps.prompt: When is this money needed? Swipe each item to the left or to the right.

items.text: Three months of costs if a job ends

steps.explanation: Money you need soon has a short [[time-horizon]]. It must be there, whatever prices do. Money that can wait for decades has time to recover from falls.

steps.prompt: True or false: an emergency fund should grow as fast as possible.
steps.explanation: False. An emergency fund must be there when something goes wrong. Investments can be down at exactly that moment. So the fund sits where its value cannot fall, even if it earns little.

steps.prompt: A job ends. At the same time, investments are down 20%. Where is the emergency fund most useful?
options: In a savings account, where its value did not fall
In a stock fund, where it lost 20%
Half in each, so half of it lost value
steps.explanation: Job losses and market falls often happen at the same time. In a savings account, the full amount is there when you need it.

steps.title: How long your savings last
steps.body: You spend about **{monthlySpending}** a month. Your savings account holds **{savingsBalance}**. That covers about **{bufferMonths}** months of costs.

steps.title: Your decision
steps.body: Your savings cover about **{bufferMonths}** months of your costs today. How many months of costs do you want to keep as your emergency fund? You choose the number.
steps.bodyNoData: How many months of your costs do you want to keep as your emergency fund? You choose the number.
